title: CTR by device
context: Does search behaviour differ by device?
task: Return device and ctr_pct = AVG(clicked) * 100 (1 decimal) from searches joined to users.
answer: SELECT u.device, ROUND(AVG(s.clicked) * 100, 1) AS ctr_pct FROM searches s JOIN users u ON u.user_id = s.user_id GROUP BY u.device;

title: Campaign performance summary
context: The advertiser dashboard row.
task: Return advertiser, impressions, clicks, ctr_pct (1 dp), spend (2 dp) per campaign.
answer: SELECT c.advertiser, COUNT(*) AS impressions, SUM(i.clicked) AS clicks, ROUND(AVG(i.clicked) * 100, 1) AS ctr_pct, ROUND(SUM(i.cost), 2) AS spend FROM ad_impressions i JOIN ad_campaigns c ON c.campaign_id = i.campaign_id GROUP BY c.campaign_id;

title: Cost per click
context: Average CPC actually paid.
task: Return advertiser and cpc (2 dp) = SUM(cost) / SUM(clicked) for campaigns with at least one click.
answer: SELECT c.advertiser, ROUND(SUM(i.cost) / SUM(i.clicked), 2) AS cpc FROM ad_impressions i JOIN ad_campaigns c ON c.campaign_id = i.campaign_id GROUP BY c.campaign_id HAVING SUM(i.clicked) > 0;

title: Cost per conversion
context: What does each conversion cost the advertiser?
task: Return advertiser and cpa (2 dp) = SUM(cost) / SUM(converted) for campaigns with at least one conversion.
answer: SELECT c.advertiser, ROUND(SUM(i.cost) / SUM(i.converted), 2) AS cpa FROM ad_impressions i JOIN ad_campaigns c ON c.campaign_id = i.campaign_id GROUP BY c.campaign_id HAVING SUM(i.converted) > 0;

title: ROAS
context: Return on ad spend = revenue / cost.
task: Return advertiser and roas (2 dp) = SUM(revenue) / SUM(cost) for campaigns with spend > 0, ordered by roas descending then advertiser.
answer: SELECT c.advertiser, ROUND(SUM(i.revenue) / SUM(i.cost), 2) AS roas FROM ad_impressions i JOIN ad_campaigns c ON c.campaign_id = i.campaign_id GROUP BY c.campaign_id HAVING SUM(i.cost) > 0 ORDER BY roas DESC, c.advertiser;

title: Budget utilisation
context: How much of each budget has been spent?
task: Return advertiser, budget, spend (2 dp) and used_pct (1 dp) = spend / budget * 100.
answer: SELECT c.advertiser, c.budget, ROUND(SUM(i.cost), 2) AS spend, ROUND(SUM(i.cost) * 100.0 / c.budget, 1) AS used_pct FROM ad_impressions i JOIN ad_campaigns c ON c.campaign_id = i.campaign_id GROUP BY c.campaign_id;

title: Bids above max CPC
context: An actual click cost should never exceed max_cpc.
task: Return impression_id, cost and max_cpc where cost > max_cpc.
answer: SELECT i.impression_id, i.cost, c.max_cpc FROM ad_impressions i JOIN ad_campaigns c ON c.campaign_id = i.campaign_id WHERE i.cost > c.max_cpc;

title: Impressions outside the flight dates
context: Ads served before start or after end.
task: Return impression_id, impression_date, start_date, end_date where impression_date < start_date OR impression_date > end_date.
answer: SELECT i.impression_id, i.impression_date, c.start_date, c.end_date FROM ad_impressions i JOIN ad_campaigns c ON c.campaign_id = i.campaign_id WHERE i.impression_date < c.start_date OR i.impression_date > c.end_date;

title: Conversions without clicks
context: A conversion can't happen without a click.
task: Return impression_id where converted = 1 and clicked = 0.
answer: SELECT impression_id FROM ad_impressions WHERE converted = 1 AND clicked = 0;

title: Campaigns with no impressions
context: Approved but never served.
task: Return advertiser and status for campaigns with no rows in ad_impressions.
answer: SELECT c.advertiser, c.status FROM ad_campaigns c LEFT JOIN ad_impressions i ON i.campaign_id = c.campaign_id WHERE i.impression_id IS NULL;

title: Users who never searched
context: Signed up, never used search.
task: Return user_id and email for users with no searches.
answer: SELECT u.user_id, u.email FROM users u LEFT JOIN searches s ON s.user_id = u.user_id WHERE s.search_id IS NULL;

title: Managers and their team size
context: Span of control, including managers with nobody.
task: Return manager name (as manager) and reports = number of employees whose manager_id is that employee, for employees at level 'L6' or 'L7'.
answer: SELECT m.name AS manager, COUNT(e.employee_id) AS reports FROM employees m LEFT JOIN employees e ON e.manager_id = m.employee_id WHERE m.level IN ('L6','L7') GROUP BY m.employee_id;

title: Employee with manager name
context: Org directory.
task: Return employee name (as employee) and manager name (as manager) for every employee that has a manager.
answer: SELECT e.name AS employee, m.name AS manager FROM employees e JOIN employees m ON m.employee_id = e.manager_id;

title: Earning more than your manager
context: Pay inversions.
task: Return employee name (as employee), salary and manager_salary where the employee earns more than their manager.
answer: SELECT e.name AS employee, e.salary, m.salary AS manager_salary FROM employees e JOIN employees m ON m.employee_id = e.manager_id WHERE e.salary > m.salary;

title: Above-org-average salary
context: Who earns above their org's average?
task: Return name, org and salary for employees earning more than the average salary in their org.
answer: SELECT e.name, e.org, e.salary FROM employees e WHERE e.salary > (SELECT AVG(salary) FROM employees WHERE org = e.org);

title: Queries only searched once
context: Long-tail queries.
task: Return query for queries that appear exactly once in searches.
answer: SELECT query FROM searches GROUP BY query HAVING COUNT(*) = 1;

title: Users who both searched Shopping and clicked a Shopping ad
context: Intent-to-ad match.
task: Return user_id for users with a search in category 'Shopping' and a clicked impression on a 'Shopping' campaign.
answer: SELECT u.user_id FROM users u WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM searches s WHERE s.user_id = u.user_id AND s.category = 'Shopping') AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM ad_impressions i JOIN ad_campaigns c ON c.campaign_id = i.campaign_id WHERE i.user_id = u.user_id AND i.clicked = 1 AND c.category = 'Shopping');

title: Searchers never shown an ad
context: Ad coverage gap.
task: Return user_id for users with at least one search and no ad impressions.
answer: SELECT u.user_id FROM users u WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM searches s WHERE s.user_id = u.user_id) AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM ad_impressions i WHERE i.user_id = u.user_id);

title: Clicks by position, wide
context: Pivot: clicks in positions 1–4 as columns per advertiser.
task: Return advertiser, p1, p2, p3, p4 = clicks at each position.
hint: SUM(CASE WHEN position = 1 THEN clicked ELSE 0 END).
answer: SELECT c.advertiser, SUM(CASE WHEN i.position = 1 THEN i.clicked ELSE 0 END) AS p1, SUM(CASE WHEN i.position = 2 THEN i.clicked ELSE 0 END) AS p2, SUM(CASE WHEN i.position = 3 THEN i.clicked ELSE 0 END) AS p3, SUM(CASE WHEN i.position = 4 THEN i.clicked ELSE 0 END) AS p4 FROM ad_impressions i JOIN ad_campaigns c ON c.campaign_id = i.campaign_id GROUP BY c.campaign_id;

title: Zero-click share by category
context: Where do searches end without a click?
task: Return category and zero_click_pct (1 dp) = searches with clicked = 0 / all * 100.
answer: SELECT category, ROUND(AVG(1 - clicked) * 100, 1) AS zero_click_pct FROM searches GROUP BY category;

title: Searches by hour of day
context: When do people search?
task: Return hour (integer) and searches count ordered by hour.
answer: SELECT CAST(SUBSTR(search_time, 1, 2) AS INTEGER) AS hour, COUNT(*) AS searches FROM searches GROUP BY hour ORDER BY hour;

title: Daily active searchers
context: DAU for search.
task: Return search_date and dau = COUNT(DISTINCT user_id), for the 10 days with the highest dau (ties by date).
hint: GROUP BY date, ORDER BY dau DESC LIMIT 10.
answer: SELECT search_date, COUNT(DISTINCT user_id) AS dau FROM searches GROUP BY search_date ORDER BY dau DESC, search_date LIMIT 10;

title: Campaign length in days
context: Flight length per campaign.
task: Return advertiser and days = end_date − start_date (integer).
answer: SELECT advertiser, CAST(julianday(end_date) - julianday(start_date) AS INTEGER) AS days FROM ad_campaigns;

title: Days since a user's last search
context: As of 2025-07-31, how stale is each searcher?
task: Return user_id and days_since (integer) = days from MAX(search_date) to '2025-07-31'.
answer: SELECT user_id, CAST(julianday('2025-07-31') - julianday(MAX(search_date)) AS INTEGER) AS days_since FROM searches GROUP BY user_id;

title: Share of spend by category
context: Where does ad revenue come from?
task: Return category and share_pct (1 dp) = category spend / total spend * 100.
answer: WITH s AS (SELECT c.category, SUM(i.cost) AS spend FROM ad_impressions i JOIN ad_campaigns c ON c.campaign_id = i.campaign_id GROUP BY c.category) SELECT category, ROUND(spend * 100.0 / (SELECT SUM(spend) FROM s), 1) AS share_pct FROM s;

title: Search-to-ad-click funnel per country
context: Searches → ad impressions → ad clicks by country.
task: Return country, searches, impressions, ad_clicks. Aggregate searches and impressions separately to avoid fan-out.
hint: Two CTEs by country, LEFT JOIN.
answer: WITH s AS (SELECT u.country, COUNT(*) AS searches FROM searches x JOIN users u ON u.user_id = x.user_id GROUP BY u.country), a AS (SELECT u.country, COUNT(*) AS impressions, SUM(i.clicked) AS ad_clicks FROM ad_impressions i JOIN users u ON u.user_id = i.user_id GROUP BY u.country) SELECT s.country, s.searches, COALESCE(a.impressions, 0) AS impressions, COALESCE(a.ad_clicks, 0) AS ad_clicks FROM s LEFT JOIN a ON a.country = s.country;

title: Queries with poor click-through
context: Popular queries (5+ searches) with CTR under 60%.
task: Return query, searches and ctr_pct (1 dp) for queries with 5+ searches and AVG(clicked) < 0.6.
answer: SELECT query, COUNT(*) AS searches, ROUND(AVG(clicked) * 100, 1) AS ctr_pct FROM searches GROUP BY query HAVING COUNT(*) >= 5 AND AVG(clicked) < 0.6;

title: Ad frequency: users hit 5+ times by one campaign in a day
context: Frequency capping violations.
task: Return user_id, campaign_id, impression_date and impressions for groups with 5 or more impressions.
answer: SELECT user_id, campaign_id, impression_date, COUNT(*) AS impressions FROM ad_impressions GROUP BY user_id, campaign_id, impression_date HAVING COUNT(*) >= 5;

title: Categories searched but not advertised
context: Demand without supply.
task: Return category values in searches that don't appear in ad_campaigns.
answer: SELECT category FROM searches EXCEPT SELECT category FROM ad_campaigns;

title: All locations in use
context: Employee locations and user countries as one list, tagged.
task: Return place and kind ('office' for employee locations, 'market' for user countries), distinct, ordered by kind then place.
answer: SELECT DISTINCT location AS place, 'office' AS kind FROM employees UNION SELECT DISTINCT country, 'market' FROM users ORDER BY kind, place;

title: Top campaign per category by conversions
context: Category winners.
task: Return category, advertiser and conversions for the campaign with the most conversions in each category (ties by advertiser).
hint: ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY category ORDER BY conversions DESC).
answer: WITH c AS (SELECT a.category, a.advertiser, SUM(i.converted) AS conversions FROM ad_impressions i JOIN ad_campaigns a ON a.campaign_id = i.campaign_id GROUP BY a.campaign_id) SELECT category, advertiser, conversions FROM (SELECT *, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY category ORDER BY conversions DESC, advertiser) AS rn FROM c) WHERE rn = 1;

title: Manager name or 'none'
context: Directory with a fallback.
task: Return employee name (as employee) and manager = COALESCE(manager's name, 'none') for every employee.
answer: SELECT e.name AS employee, COALESCE(m.name, 'none') AS manager FROM employees e LEFT JOIN employees m ON m.employee_id = e.manager_id;

title: First word of each query
context: Query intent often lives in the first word.
task: Return first_word and searches count, top 5 by count (ties by word).
answer: SELECT SUBSTR(query, 1, INSTR(query || ' ', ' ') - 1) AS first_word, COUNT(*) AS searches FROM searches GROUP BY first_word ORDER BY searches DESC, first_word LIMIT 5;
